perspective:
Harold’s accessible information:

- He is a Project Manager whose project progress is suffering. He feels frustrated and anxious and believes his team is unmotivated.
- He arranges and attends a coffee-shop meeting with his friend Arthur Begum. He tells Arthur he needs advice because his team seems unmotivated and it is affecting progress.
- He hears Arthur advise him to understand what drives each team member individually, have one-on-one conversations, and help people feel valued and understood.
- Harold tells Arthur he had not really done that, having focused on goals and deadlines, and agrees to try it. He thanks Arthur and feels more hopeful.
- After the meeting, Harold feels hopeful and relieved and believes Arthur’s advice will help. In a team meeting, he tells the team he wants one-on-one chats to understand their motivations.
- He hears Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time with each of them.
- Later, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well to the new strategies. He feels disappointed and worried and tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still isn’t responding.
- He hears Arthur say there may be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold says he will set up another round of meetings and thanks Arthur.
- Harold becomes determined and focused and believes there may be underlying team issues. He holds one-on-one meetings and asks team members to share concerns.
- He hears Team Member 1 say there has been tension between a few members affecting work. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed with the workload and stressed.
- Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts and see if tasks can be redistributed, and that their well-being is important.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered and believes addressing individual concerns will improve performance. He tells the team they will have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He hears Team Member 1 say that sounds great and will help, and Team Member 2 agree that it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and that their input and well-being are crucial.

He does not have access to hidden thoughts, private motives, or unobserved events beyond what he directly experienced, observed, or was told.
